name: v1_encode_v2_decode_appended_field
schema_v1:
namespace test.evo
message M { x @0 : u32 }
schema_v2:
namespace test.evo
message M { x @0 : u32  y @1 : u16 }
notes: The bytes are unchanged historical evidence. A strict v2 decoder reaches EOF before required y; EOF is not a general evolution signal.

name: v2_encode_v1_decode_trailing_ignored
schema_v1:
namespace test.evo
message M { x @0 : u32 }
schema_v2:
namespace test.evo
message M { x @0 : u32  y @1 : u16 }
notes: A bounded top-level v1 reader can stop after x, but nested and aggregate message values have no boundary that identifies y as trailing data.

name: v1_encode_v2_decode_appended_optional_field
schema_v1:
namespace test.evo
message M { x @0 : u32 }
schema_v2:
namespace test.evo
message M { x @0 : u32  y @1 : optional<u16> }
notes: Some top-level readers may treat EOF as an absent optional, but an inline decoder can consume a parent or following value as the presence bit.

name: v2_encode_v1_decode_appended_optional_field
schema_v1:
namespace test.evo
message M { x @0 : u32 }
schema_v2:
namespace test.evo
message M { x @0 : u32  y @1 : optional<u16> }
notes: Stopping after x is observable only when the caller already owns the message boundary; it is not a reusable message compatibility guarantee.

name: appended_nested_field_consumes_parent_field
notes: A v2 Inner decoder sees the v1 parent field z byte where it expects appended y. No internal length separates the nested value from its parent.

name: appended_sub_byte_default_matches_old_padding
schema_v1:
namespace test.evo
message M { x @0 : u4 }
schema_v2:
namespace test.evo
message M { x @0 : u4  y @1 : u4 }
notes: Old padding and an appended zero-valued u4 produce identical bytes, so payload bytes alone do not identify the schema version or field boundary.
